Building the south pole…

Moon Base, Ten Years On

A walkthrough of the lunar south pole, ten years on (optimistic scenario)

It is March 2037, a little over ten years from now, at the start of southern summer at the pole. This scenario assumes NASA's 2026 Moon Base plan ran on schedule: robotic scouting, then infrastructure from 2029, then permanent habitats from 2032. The tour covers 15 stops: landing pads, solar towers, fission reactors, the habitats and their interior, rovers, and an ice plant on the rim of Shackleton crater. It ends with a visit to an imagined China-led ILRS station 38 km away.

The Sun, Earth and stars are computed for the real dates. Earth shows its true face and phase. Shackleton, de Gerlache and the surrounding craters sit at their real positions. The local terrain and all the hardware are invented, based on published plans and concept art.

Desktop: click to look · WASD to walk · Shift to lope · Space to jump (1.62 m/s² gravity) · N/P for tour stops · [ ] to change time · L for labels · H to hide the HUD · F to fly (E/Q up/down) · E next to a Lunar Terrain Vehicle to drive it (W/S throttle, A/D steer, Shift ×3, C chase view).
VR: right/left trigger for next/previous stop · left stick to walk · right stick to turn · A to jump · B for labels · X/Y to change time by 6 h · grip next to an LTV to drive it (left stick). Read the tour text on your left wrist.
